# `ssh` check

Check that an SSH server answers, and optionally that key authentication works.

```yaml
checks:
  example:
    type: ssh
    target: bastion.example.com:22
    auth: true
    user: deploy
    key: ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```

## Keys

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` **(required)** | string |  | host or host:port (port defaults to 22). |
| `auth` | bool | `false` | Log in with a key to prove authentication works (requires user and key). |
| `user` | string |  | User for auth. |
| `key` | string |  | Private key file for auth (unencrypted; ~ is expanded). |
| `known_hosts` | string |  | known_hosts file used to verify the host key during auth (default ~/.ssh/known_hosts). |
| `insecure` | bool | `false` | Skip host key verification during auth (shown in the report). Avoid. |
| `expect` | mapping |  | What counts as healthy. |
| `expect.banner_contains` | string |  | Text the server version banner must contain (e.g. OpenSSH). |

Every check also accepts the [common keys](../config.md#common-check-keys).

One-liner: `medic check ssh <target> [--set key=value ...]`
